$comment: DISTRIBUTION LOG. One row per act of publishing. Not a CRM: nine fields, no contacts, no pipeline, no personal data.
status: planned -> published | skipped | blocked. Fill date and result AFTER publishing; never before.
attribution is null where the channel carries no tracked link on purpose (community, outreach). That is a decision, not a gap -- see README.md section 5.
Rows for days 1-14 were DERIVED from marketing/content/register.json rather than typed, so the two cannot disagree.
Validated by `pnpm check:distribution`, which re-derives every field from the content register and the site routes and fails on any drift.
Append rows for days 15-30 when those days are reached. This file is a log, not a plan: marketing/content/calendar.md is the schedule.

amplification is a SEPARATE log for paid promotion of an already-published asset. It is not a row, because a boost is not an act of publishing, and it never changes the organic row's date, result or copy. The row points at it so its counts cannot be read as organic-only. Unknowns stay null: a guessed spend or boost window is worse than an absent one.

rowShape.date: YYYY-MM-DD, the day it actually went out. null while planned
rowShape.day: day offset from marketing/content/calendar.md, or null for opportunistic work
rowShape.channel: linkedin | x | devto | hashnode | github | community | outreach
rowShape.destination: a route that exists in apps/web/src/app, or null
rowShape.icpHypothesis: p1 | p2 | neutral. Which MESSAGE was tested, never who the reader is (analytics.md section 9)
rowShape.pillar: a | b | c | d | e | f | g, from CONTENT-PILLARS.md
rowShape.attribution: the utm quartet, or null where the channel carries no tracked link by design
rowShape.result: free text, written after. Absolute counts only until analytics.md section 10's baseline window closes

amplificationShape.id: amp-NNN, referenced by the `amplification` field on the row it amplifies
amplificationShape.asset: an id from marketing/content/register.json, and it must already be published
amplificationShape.channel: same vocabulary as a row's channel
amplificationShape.durationDays: whole days the amplification runs, or null if not known
amplificationShape.spend: an object once the platform reports it, else null. NEVER guessed
amplificationShape.platformMetrics: impressions/clicks/CPM/CPC/CTR as the platform reports them, else null. NEVER guessed
amplificationShape.note: free text. Must carry the measurement rule: traffic during the window is not purely organic

amplification.note: Paid amplification of the ALREADY-PUBLISHED LI-003. This is not a second act of publishing and not a new asset: the organic row keeps its own date, result and copy. Only four facts are known and recorded — the asset, the channel, that it is a boosted post, and that it runs four days. Start and end dates, spend, impressions, clicks, CPM, CPC, CTR, audience settings and any LinkedIn campaign id are NOT known and are left null rather than guessed. MEASUREMENT RULE: arrivals during the boost window are not purely organic LI-003 performance and must never be reported as such. Two things follow. First, it is not known whether the counts already recorded on the organic row fall inside the boost window, so they cannot be called organic-only either. Second, a LinkedIn boost normally promotes the original post, which carries the original tagged URL — so paid and organic arrivals reach us with the same kx_source, kx_campaign and kx_content and are INDISTINGUISHABLE in first-party data. Unless a separate tagged URL was used, the end-of-boost comparison can set LinkedIn's reported figures beside our session counts, but cannot split our sessions into paid and organic. Confirm which link the boost served before any such comparison.

$notYetRoutes: Routes named in the distribution documents BECAUSE they do not exist yet. /blog is the seo.md decision: no blog until three articles have run off-site and one shows traffic. Anything else naming a missing route is a defect.

rows.result: 5 sessions carried kx_p2_a_drift; 1 reached Qualified Evaluation; 0 reached Adoption Intent. Attribution pipeline confirmed working end to end — campaign, medium and content arrived intact, and the funnel vocabulary was already deployed (#253, 2026-09-29 12:43 UTC). One early session recorded kx_source=other while campaign, medium and content survived; the register's own URL cannot produce that, so a variant link was used for that click. The raw value is discarded by design and was not recovered, and this is logged as a single observation, not a defect. Absolute counts only — analytics.md §10's baseline window is open, so no rate is computed and no conclusion drawn.

rows.metricToWatch: whether kx_source=x produces any session at all
rows.result: 2 sessions carried kx_p2_a_drift with utm_content=x_single; 0 reached Qualified Evaluation; 0 reached Adoption Intent. Logged the same day it posted, so these are early counts and not a settled figure. The metric to watch was whether kx_source=x produces a session at all: it did — 1 of the 2 resolved to x, the other to `other`, the same fallback one day-1 session hit. Both carried a correct medium, campaign and content and arrived with no referrer, so only utm_source failed to resolve; the register's own URL cannot produce that. Link hygiene to watch, not an instrumentation change — the raw value is discarded by design and was not recovered. Absolute counts only — analytics.md §10's baseline window is open, so no rate is computed and no conclusion drawn.
